claim: In §19.2, with semantically plural predicands in ascriptive constructions lacking explicit quantification, rule [12] assigns non-distributive interpretation to singular predicatives.
evidence_summary: “Coin envelopes are a good size for most seeds” describes the individual envelopes. Give a seedling a 10-cm pot and a tree a 40-cm pot. “The pots are a suitable size for their respective plants” can be true. In that context the unmarked “These pots are a suitable size” can also be true, then false after swapping the plants.
finding: Suitability applies separately to each pot although the predicative NP is singular and their sizes differ. A single shared value is possible but unnecessary. The argument against general grammatical number concord survives.
proposed_wording: With a semantically plural predicand, a singular predicative may attribute a property to the group or to each member. In the latter case each member may satisfy the description with a different value.
inference: Does a singular count predicative force the property to apply to the bearers collectively?

evidence.source: Mikaela Boley (2020). Collecting Native Seed. University of Maryland Extension.
evidence.passage: §19.2, p. 513, [12], following [11i–ii]. The rule assigns plural forms distributively and “singular forms non-distributively”. Its domain excludes specifying predicatives and explicit quantification. The quantified cases are taken up on p. 515.
evidence.example: “Coin envelopes are a good size for most seeds.” The advice concerns which individual envelopes can hold the material. The dimensions of a stack would not answer that question.
evidence.establishes: A singular predicative is applicable to individual bearers. The different-sized pots in the audit test the further suggestion that those bearers have to share one value.
evidence.locator: Handout p. 9, Taking Care of Collected Seed, first bullet.
